ai.name: Prime Intellect
ai.hook: New agent-training stack makes 40-turn coding agents practical to train at scale.
insights: **verifiers v1** stores rollout traces as **message DAGs**, cutting complexity from **O(n²) to O(n)**
Demonstrated a **100B reasoning model** running **40-turn SWE agent tasks** on just **6 H200 nodes** in under 2 days
Ships with **vLLM** integration to avoid tokenization drift during rollouts
ai.for_you: No direct action here, this is infra for training frontier models, filed for awareness of where agent tooling is heading.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only genuine technical release today, not just another model launch recap

ai.name: Anthropic
ai.hook: Anthropic's 'Jacobian lens' shows Claude visibly pausing to reason before answering.
insights: The tool traces internal activation patterns while Claude works through a task, not just its final output
Researchers found both mundane reasoning traces and some unnerving ones they can't fully explain yet
Comes as Anthropic sits near a **$1 trillion valuation**, giving this kind of interpretability work outsized attention
ai.for_you: No direct action, but worth 10 minutes: this is the clearest public example yet of *why* a model's output looks the way it does, useful vocabulary when a PT SMB client asks 'can you trust it'.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most substantive interpretability story of the week, not a product launch

ai.name: Simon Willison
ai.hook: Someone built a playable Doom clone where SQLite is the entire game engine.
insights: **DOOMQL**: movement, collision, enemies, combat, and every pixel are driven by SQL queries, not code logic
Built entirely with **GPT-5.6 Sol** as a Python terminal script
Runs by just cloning the repo, no special setup described
ai.for_you: Good 20-minute weekend curiosity to see what GPT-5.6 can one-shot on a weird constraint, not a client deliverable but useful gut-check on current model ceiling.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most concrete, playable proof-of-capability example today vs. abstract benchmark talk

ai.name: Dan Biderman
ai.role: Co-founder & CEO · Engram (No Priors / Latent Space)
ai.hook: Long context and RAG both break down at scale, Engram bets on compressing knowledge into model weights instead.
insights: Engram raised **$98M** to build 'knowledge cartridges' that compress company/personal data directly into weights rather than stuffing context windows
Argues **context rot** hits hard at trillion-token company knowledge bases, long context alone won't solve enterprise memory
Frames personal AI models as improving like **'Tamagotchis'**, continuously updated from user feedback loops
ai.for_you: Relevant if the micro-SaaS idea ever touches 'AI that remembers you': the pitch here is that stuffing more context isn't the long-term answer, memory needs to live in weights, worth filing as a differentiator narrative if you pitch a personalized AI tool later.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Best concrete technical framework in podcasts this week, not just a founder story

ai.name: Andrej Karpathy
ai.hook: Karpathy says context windows are a cheap hack, not real model customization.
insights: Argues fine-tuning without losing base capabilities is far trickier than most people assume
Calls the 'science of manipulating brains' (i.e. steering model behavior reliably) still immature
ai.for_you: Directly relevant to how you scope AI agency deliverables for PT SMBs: promising a client a 'custom-trained' model is riskier and less controllable than a well-designed prompt/context layer, set expectations accordingly.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Karpathy's clearest public statement this week on fine-tuning risk vs. hype

ai.name: OpenAI vs Anthropic
ai.hook: Codex usage jumped 10x in six months to 7M users, may have overtaken Claude Code.
insights: Codex added **+1M users in roughly one day** during the tracking window
Coincides with OpenAI merging Codex into the ChatGPT desktop app as a 'superapp' move
Claude Code has gone quiet on public usage reporting during the same period
ai.for_you: Signals which coding agent your agency should default to recommending/building on for client automation work, Codex's growth curve now rivals or beats Claude Code's.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Concrete usage numbers beat another vague 'quiet day' recap

build_this.name: Clawk
build_this.what_it_is: Gives coding agents a disposable Linux VM to run in instead of your actual laptop.
build_this.why_try_it: Useful if you start letting Claude/Codex agents run more autonomous tasks for agency client projects, this sandboxes risky agent actions (installing packages, running scripts) away from your real machine before you trust the output.

build_this.name: Jacquard
build_this.what_it_is: A programming language explicitly designed for AI-written, human-reviewed code.
build_this.why_try_it: Worth a skim this week as a concept, not a build, since it directly touches your 'not a developer yet but building real products' position: it's an early attempt at making AI-generated code easier for non-experts to audit and trust before shipping.

build_this.name: prompts.chat
build_this.what_it_is: Self-hostable, open-source library of community prompts (formerly Awesome ChatGPT Prompts).
build_this.why_try_it: Fork and curate a private version for the AI agency: pre-load PT SMB-specific prompt templates (invoicing, customer support replies, social copy in PT-PT) as a reusable asset you hand to every new client instead of rebuilding from scratch.
